ticket.title: miter clones --across-crates: group duplication by crate pair
ticket.description: Remaining half of GB-164 after outfeed gate moved to OF-37. miter clones currently groups by file; grouping by crate pair is the strongest evidence available for a shared crate - two crates sharing a few hundred lines is exactly what justifies an extraction, and it is the one input GB-160 currently has to infer. Add --across-crates to emit a matrix of crate pairs with shared-clone counts and the source spans involved, so MTR-13 --what-if can cite duplication as evidence rather than assertion.

task.title: miter clones --across-crates plus an outfeed gate that runs the Tier 3 matrix
task.description: Two dogfooding wins surfaced while auditing, batched because both are small and independent. (1) miter clones --across-crates: group duplication by crate pair instead of by file. Two crates sharing three hundred lines is the strongest evidence available for a shared crate, and it is the one input GB-160 currently has to guess at. (2) outfeed gate: one command running the Tier 3 matrix - cargo fmt --check, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, nextest --workspace, miter contracts, outfeed lockfiles, chalkline docs check --workspace - so the release gate stops being typed by hand. Motivation is first-hand: today produced a commit that left Cargo.lock unstaged and one that briefly broke a #[cfg(test)] pairing, both inside manually assembled gate commands.
